hypothesis: At least 95% of genuine 8-20 word quotes containing curly quotes/apostrophes or en/em dashes still verify after those characters are folded to ASCII (' " -).
limitations: Only quote-mark and dash folding is tested; ellipses, ligatures, non-breaking spaces and Unicode normalization forms are not.
Whether the gate should tolerate typography is a product decision; this measures behaviour, it does not decide policy.
The corpus is the repository's papers/ snapshot.

metrics.description: Windows with curly quotes accepted after folding quotes only.
metrics.name: quote_mark_variant_acceptance_rate

metrics.description: Windows with en/em dashes accepted after folding dashes only.
metrics.name: dash_variant_acceptance_rate

metrics.description: Windows skipped because the folded text already exists in the corpus.
metrics.name: excluded_ascii_form_present

metrics.description: Median wall time of one verify_quote call.
metrics.name: median_verify_latency_ms

procedure: Load and hash the papers/ corpus as in V3D-EXP-0001.
Find every token containing a curly quote/apostrophe or en/em dash; with the seed, sample up to 50 distinct 8-20 word windows around them.
Exclude windows whose ASCII-folded form already occurs verbatim somewhere in the corpus (counted).
Verify the unmodified window (control), the fully folded window, and quote-only / dash-only folded variants.
Store the full case table as an artifact.
question: Does verify_quote still accept a genuine quote when only its typography differs from the source, as happens when a model straightens curly quotes or writes hyphens for dashes?
rationale: Models commonly normalize typography when reproducing text. If the gate rejects such quotes, faithful citations are shown as ungrounded (false negatives), which erodes trust in the grounding label.
title: Citation gate tolerates typographic normalization of genuine quotes
